grading.criterionPass: All semantically required components of a criterion must be correct and supported by appropriate cited source evidence; wording may vary.
grading.fullyCorrect: All four binary criteria pass AND no critical false claim.
grading.criticalGate: A materially asserted listed critical false claim fails fullyCorrect even when other criteria pass. Absence of an optional detail is not a false claim.
grading.aggregate: Report per-task 0-4 required criteria plus fullyCorrect 0/1 and criticalFalseClaim 0/1. Never compute a quality-adjusted speed number by dropping failures.
grading.testEvidence: Existing test definitions are source evidence only. This suite requires no test execution.

criteria.requirement: For the registered method/tree, malformed decoding reaches _onBadUrl. With onBadUrl, find returns a non-null handle whose handler defers invoking onBadUrl; find itself does not invoke it.
lookup derives constraints, calls find, then callHandler. A supplied onBadUrl runs with the malformed path, req and res, rather than defaultRoute; cite the lookup test's /hello/%world assertion.
Without onBadUrl, _onBadUrl returns null; direct find returns null while lookup calls configured defaultRoute. With no defaultRoute, response becomes status 404 and end() is called.

Cite the README's malformed URL default/onBadUrl description and explain its request-dispatch behavior in relation to the distinct direct-find tests; do not treat README example's 400 as an automatic library status.

criticalFalseClaims: find directly invokes configured defaultRoute or onBadUrl
Library automatically returns status 400 merely because onBadUrl is configured
Malformed request invokes registered ordinary route handler in this scenario

criteria.requirement: compile replaces instance find and lookup with _findCompiled and _lookupCompiled and compiles existing method trees; synchronous compiled lookup calls compiled.lookup directly after deriving constraints.

A third-argument function or supplied done takes _lookupCompiled's Router.prototype.lookup.call fallback. That method normalizes ctx/done and derives constraints using a callback; derive error goes to done(err).

After asynchronous derivation, the fallback uses this.find (therefore compiled find after compile), then this.callHandler and done(null,result); callHandler uses returned handle.handler, or default route for null. Request-derived constraints/user callbacks determine selected handler; exact arbitrary application handler is not statically fixed.

Identify compile.test.js asynchronous test: user deriveConstraint setImmediate reads x-secret, two same-path alpha/beta constraints, request beta yields beta, no error, lookup remains _lookupCompiled.

criticalFalseClaims: Supplying a done callback bypasses constraint derivation
All compiled lookup calls directly invoke compiled.lookup with no fallback
The named application's callback or runtime route can be uniquely determined from a static call edge alone

criteria.requirement: matches_into constructs Candidate and delegates to matches_candidate_into, which clears the existing Vec before checking empty set; no matches or an empty set leaves the buffer empty rather than retaining old contents.

Results are zero-based original pattern sequence/insertion indices, in ascending order with duplicate indices removed; not strategy iteration order, match positions, or ranking. Builder pushes patterns; build delegates to GlobSet::new, whose enumerate indices feed strategies.

Matching visits every strategy and accumulates then sort/dedup, while matches allocates a fresh vector via matches_candidate and reaches same collector for nonempty sets. Explain how reusable caller storage avoids requiring matches' new result allocation.

Identify set_works test: patterns src/**/*.rs, *.c, src/lib.rs, matching src/lib.rs returns indices 0 and 2. Attribute buffer clearing/empty-buffer/order contract to implementation/API docs, without claiming this test directly checks reused prefilled buffers.

criticalFalseClaims: matches_into preserves/appends prior vector entries
Indices are sorted by specificity or are 1-based
dedup means identical patterns can never have distinct insertion indices
Existing set_works test directly tests a reused prefilled Vec

criteria.requirement: literal_separator defaults false, so ordinary * and ? can match slash; use GlobBuilder.literal_separator(true) before build to prohibit separators for these wildcard tokens.

Builder stores option; token regex generation uses [^/]/[^/]* with literal_separator enabled and ./.* otherwise. Thus some/*/needle.txt is bounded to the intermediate component in the stated configuration.

Explicit recursive **/ or /**/ tokens have their own generation, unaffected by the ordinary wildcard branch; public syntax documents zero-or-more directories for /**/. Use some/**/needle.txt for zero or multiple intervening directories.

Cite positive recursive matchrec1-3 and negative SLASHLIT some/* cases matchrec31/32 (or equally relevant slash tests); note test macros build ordinary, strategic, and GlobSet matchers, so cited tests check actual matching behavior rather than only generated regex text.

criticalFalseClaims: literal_separator is enabled by default
literal_separator(true) prevents all recursive ** matching
Single-star necessarily has shell's separator semantics regardless of configuration

criteria.requirement: Root PersistentPreRunE rejects only when IsAuthCheckEnabled && !CheckAuth; CheckAuth passes from HasEnvToken or nonempty configured Hosts. This function is a local presence/configuration gate, not a network validation of token correctness.

Help/completion names bypass; command annotation on command or visited non-root ancestor disables check; a flagged exemption applies to a set flag (Flags.Visit), not merely registration. Cite Test_IsAuthCheckEnabled cases distinguishing flag set and unset.

Rejection prints codespace-scope login for direct parent Use codespace; otherwise authHelp prioritizes GITHUB_ACTIONS == true, then nonempty CI, then interactive login/token help, and root returns AuthError.

Identify Test_CheckAuth no-known-host/no-token false, environment GITHUB_TOKEN true, known host true, enterprise token true; cite focused source test. Cite existing exemption tests (command, unset flag, set flag) rather than claiming root integration/network tests were run.

criticalFalseClaims: CheckAuth makes a network request to validate credentials
Merely registering an exempt flag always skips authentication
All root commands always require stored credentials
CI help takes priority over GITHUB_ACTIONS=true

criteria.requirement: Root selects shell constructor for valid configured expansion starting !, otherwise regular constructor. Regular RunE calls expandAlias, sets root args, and root.Execute; shell RunE calls expandShellAlias then exec.Command/PrepareCmd.Run with IO streams.

Regular expansion substitutes numbered placeholders, shell-splits result and appends trailing extra args. Use test's issue list --author=$1 --label=$2 with vilmibm,epic,-R,monalisa/testing giving author/label plus trailing -R monalisa/testing; remaining $digit returns not-enough-arguments error.

Shell expansion finds sh, strips leading !, creates [sh,-c,script] and if args adds -- then original args rather than Go performing numbered substitutions. Cite shell test expected /usr/bin/sh,-c,git branch checkout,--,123.

Shell discovery failure propagates without execution; cite unable-to-find-sh test. Shell process exit error is wrapped ExternalCommandExitError; other execution errors wrapped failed-to-run message. Regular and shell aliases disable flag parsing and auth check.

criticalFalseClaims: Regular aliases always spawn a shell
Shell aliases use expandAlias's Go numbered replacement algorithm
Unavailable shell silently falls back to regular alias execution
Missing regular positional arguments are silently ignored
